title: Low-cost config risk calibration and evaluation plan
content:
Purpose and context:

This note captures an actionable eval plan and spreadsheet layout to calibrate quality gates for lower-cost serving configurations (quantized/fast variants, smaller context, aggressive batching). Goal is to produce deterministic, reviewable gate thresholds that limit regressions while enabling ~15–40% unit-cost savings where appropriate. This document is intentionally pragmatic — lightweight sampling + conservative pass criteria to avoid customer-visible regressions.

Audience:
- Product-optimize owners
- Applied ML + Eval team
- Serving-runtime and Release engineers responsible for rollouts

Assumptions and constraints:
- Baseline = current default production variant for a given model (e.g., rwk-70b-fp16).
- Candidate = low-cost variant (e.g., rwk-70b-4bit, smaller context, or smaller model).
- We care about both aggregate quality deltas and tail/regression slices (sensitive intents).
- Unit cost is computed from infra cost-per-GPU-hour + observed tokens/sec; we use normalized cost-per-1k-tokens for comparability.

High-level proposal:
1) Standard spreadsheet that computes per-config economics and quality delta per slice.
2) A two-tier gate: (A) quick automated gate for rollout eligibility based on coarse sampling; (B) deeper gate for scaling beyond canary based on stratified evals and slice-level criteria.
3) Conservative defaults for pass/fail; teams can propose relaxed thresholds with compensating mitigations (shorter rollout, increased monitoring, immediate fallback).

Spreadsheet layout (columns) — canonical representation for each config tested:
- config_id
- model_family
- variant_notes (quant, batch, ctx_len)
- measured_p50_latency_ms
- measured_p95_latency_ms
- avg_tokens_per_request
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
- cost_per_request_usd (derived = avg_tokens/1k * cost_per_1k)
- baseline_quality_score (macro metric e.g., BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim or composite eval score)
- candidate_quality_score
- delta_quality_vs_baseline (candidate - baseline)
- relative_cost_savings_pct (1 - candidate_cost / baseline_cost)
- regression_slices_failed_count
- total_slices_evaluated
- slice_fail_rate (regression_slices_failed_count / total_slices_evaluated)
- recommended_action (auto-pass | canary-only | blocked)
- notes

Key formulas and examples:
- cost_per_request_usd = avg_tokens_per_request / 1000 * cost_per_1k_tokens_usd
- relative_cost_savings_pct = (baseline_cost_per_request - candidate_cost_per_request) / baseline_cost_per_request * 100
- delta_quality_vs_baseline = candidate_quality_score - baseline_quality_score (positive = better)

Sample row (illustrative):
- config_id: low-q4-ctx2-1
- model_family: rwk-70b
- variant_notes: 4-bit, ctx=2k, batch=auto
- measured_p50_latency_ms: 120
- measured_p95_latency_ms: 350
- avg_tokens_per_request: 250
- cost_per_1k_tokens_usd: 0.0034
- cost_per_request_usd: 0.00085
- baseline_quality_score: 0.812
- candidate_quality_score: 0.793
- delta_quality_vs_baseline: -0.019
- relative_cost_savings_pct: 22.4%
- regression_slices_failed_count: 6
- total_slices_evaluated: 120
- slice_fail_rate: 5.0%
- recommended_action: canary-only
- notes: acceptable for low-risk features; fails on dialogue-continuity slice

Gate definitions (conservative defaults):
Automated quick gate (pre-canary):
- Minimum sample size: 500 examples sampled uniformly from production logs (de-identified).
- Aggregate quality delta must be >= -0.015 (i.e., candidate not worse by more than 1.5 percentage points on composite score).
- Overall slice_fail_rate must be <= 3% across the canonical slice set (see SLICES below).
- Relative_cost_savings_pct must be >= 10% to justify complexity.
- If any single high-sensitivity slice (legal/medical/semantic-constraint) fails > 1% -> auto-block.

Deeper gate (post-canary, before broad rollout):
- Stratified sample size: 2k examples, weighted by traffic share and slice importance.
- delta_quality_vs_baseline >= -0.01 (stricter)
- No slice with delta_quality_vs_baseline < -0.03 (i.e., no catastrophic drop in any slice).
- Observed p95 latency degradation vs baseline <= +20%.
- Error rates (generation failures, crashes, low-confidence signals) must be <= baseline + 0.5pp.

SLICES (canonical set to evaluate):
- short prompt completion (<= 32 tokens)
- long context summarization (> 512 tokens)
- instruction-following (2–4 step tasks)
- dialogue-continuity (multi-turn > 3 turns)
- code-synthesis (syntactic correctness sample)
- safety/abusive-content detection (false-positive/false-negative checks)
- regulatory-sensitive (PII redaction, legal phrasing)

Decision matrix (simplified):
- Pass quick gate and deep gate -> broad rollout with staged traffic ramp.
- Pass quick gate, fail deep gate -> extended canary + targeted augment evals OR rollback to baseline for that tenant.
- Fail quick gate -> do not canary; investigate quantization/kv-cache adjustments.

Sampling and statistical notes:
- Use bootstrapped CIs for delta_quality_vs_baseline; require 95% CI lower bound > -0.03 for quick gate (i.e., we need to be 95% confident candidate is not worse than -3%).
- For slices with low event frequency, use oversampling and reweighting when computing global metrics.
- Report both absolute and relative metrics (e.g., absolute BLEU drop and percentile rank change).

Rollout playbook (practical steps):
1) Generate candidate config and collect bench numbers in lab (latency, token throughput, memory footprint).
2) Run automated quick gate against 500-sample scrubbed historical queries. Populate spreadsheet.
3) If quick gate passes, create canary build (0.5–2% traffic) with aggressive monitoring (per-slice evals, trace sampling).
4) After 48–72h with canary, run stratified eval (2k+ samples) and compute deeper gate metrics.
5) If deep gate passes, ramp to 20% then 100% with step checks; if fails at any stage, immediately fallback route to baseline variant.

Fallback and mitigation options:
- Immediate fallback to pinned baseline for affected tenant/route.
- Reduce context length or batch parameters if regression localized to long-context slices.
- Use hybrid routing: route safety/regulatory-sensitive requests to baseline while sending rest to candidate.

Monitoring knobs and dashboards to add:
- Per-config composite quality score time series (hourly)
- Per-slice fail rates and delta_quality heatmap
- Cost-per-1k-tokens by config and region
- Canary vs baseline error traces and generation confidence distributions

Open questions and tradeoffs (for discussion):
- How to weight slices in composite score? (equal weights vs traffic-weighted vs business-impact-weighted)
- When is a 10% cost saving not worth 1% quality loss? propose a default monetary conversion: $ per basis point drop in composite score computed from customer support/retention models (TBD).
- How to handle model-family drift when baseline changes frequently? suggest automating periodic recalibration windows.

Next actions (owners):
- Aisha: finalize the spreadsheet template and centralize canonical slice list (due 2026-03-05).
- Marco: implement quick-gate script to run on historical logs and output CSV matching layout (WIP, PR linked).
- Sofia: prototype dashboard panels for per-slice pass/fail and cost vs quality scatter.
- Ben: draft tenant-level routing playbook for hybrid strategies.

Appendix — minimal evaluation checklist (to attach to PR/Canary):
- [ ] CSV exported with all spreadsheet columns populated
- [ ] 500-sample quick-gate raw outputs and bootstrap CI report
- [ ] Canary telemetry enabled and alerting thresholds configured
- [ ] Rollback policy specified and tested in staging
- [ ] Linked PR and Confluence playbook referenced

End of note.

Contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) for questions or to request clarification on the defaults.
